title: Enterprise analytics request lifecycle and delivery commitments
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers frequently submit ad-hoc analytics and export requests (usage, per-route cost breakdowns, tenant-level retention snapshots) that are operationally heavy to triage. Current intake lacks consistent signal for effort, data sensitivity, and expected delivery timeline, resulting in unpredictable SLAs and friction with customer success.

Objective: Define a repeatable request lifecycle and a set of delivery commitments (SLA tiers) for console/reporting requests that balances customer expectations, engineering velocity, and cost. The solution should: (1) provide a structured intake form surfaced in the Console and via support channels, (2) classify requests into deterministic lanes with target TAT (turnaround time) and delivery format, and (3) enable routing to self-serve, automated exports, or engineering-assisted delivery.

Proposal summary:
- Intake surface: new lightweight request form in Console (Quick Analytics Request) + standardized support template. Capture: request intent, dataset(s), tenant scope (single vs multi), frequency (one-off vs scheduled), retention sensitivity (PII/risk), desired output format, business impact, and desired SLA tier.
- Triage matrix: deterministic mapping from form fields to four lanes: Self-Serve (templates/dashboards), Automated Export (scheduled CSV/Parquet), Low-touch Engineering (config + small code work), High-touch Eng + Solutions (custom ETL & legal review). Each lane has target commitments (see acceptance criteria).
- SLA tiers & commitments:
  * Bronze (Self-Serve): 0-3 business days to confirm, immediate access to templated dashboard if available.
  * Silver (Automated Export): 3-7 business days to schedule export and provide delivery URL / retention policy.
  * Gold (Low-touch Eng): 7-21 business days for engineering work, includes scope checklist and delivery estimate.
  * Platinum (High-touch): >21 days, requires AM/solutions scoping, contract/PO, and potential data-sharing agreement.
- Acceptance criteria / gating: each request must include sample query/SQL or a clearly defined metric definition, clear tenant list, and PII classification. Requests without the "minimum fields" are auto-labeled "Needs Info" and routed back to requestor with a template.
- Instrumentation: add telemetry for request counts, lane conversion rates, median time-to-commit, and rework rate (requests that move lanes). Expose a per-tenant dashboard for enterprise sales and CS to view status.
- Delivery mechanics: self-serve lane should leverage existing dashboard templates and saved queries; automated exports should reuse the export scheduling infra being scoped in PM-9814; engineering lanes will be tracked as sub-issues and scoped into Dedicated or Private work depending on data residency constraints.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict gating increases friction for low-value requests but saves engineering time; recommendation is to pilot with an aggressive "minimum fields" policy and relax based on observed false positives.
- SLA commitments introduce expectations that may require headroom; recommend aligning Silver/GOLD with current engineering capacity and reserving Platinum for contractual engagements.

Open questions:
- Should we expose SLA tier selection to the customer or infer tier from provided signals? (proposal: allow selection but validate; if they select a faster tier and we can’t meet it, escalate to AM).
- How do we price engineering-assisted deliveries — billable or included in enterprise plan? Needs GTM input.
